title: Add missing `index` parameter to mapper function in `pMapIterable` (#71)
eligibility: parent and head pinned runtime suites completed green in the frozen-order extension

review_fields.contract_or_reason: Adds the documented mapper `index` to pMapIterable, but `mapper(await value, index++)` evaluates `index++` after the element promise resolves, so with concurrency > 1 and element promises that resolve out of order, indexes follow resolution order, not source position. Promise elements are a supported input (pMap passes the source index), and the tests only use elements that resolve in order.

Error type and `.errors` are kept, but the message changes from the joined inner messages to empty, and the tests are updated to say so. This is a deliberate breaking change that goes with the engine bump.

title: Do not run mapping after stop-on-error happened (#40)
eligibility: parent and head pinned runtime suites completed green in the frozen-order extension

review_fields.contract_or_reason: After a stop-on-error rejection, a runner whose element was still pending no longer calls the mapper. That matches the stopOnError contract and the new test ([1, 3] mapped, not 2).

title: Fix `pMapIterable` not closing the source iterator when iteration stops early
eligibility: parent and head pinned runtime suites completed green in the frozen-order extension

review_fields.contract_or_reason: pMapIterable now calls the source `return()` when the consumer stops early, matching `for await`. The call is not awaited, so a source blocked in next() cannot hang the consumer, and its rejection is swallowed. Tests cover break, throw, mapper error and exhaustion.

title: Fix cleaning up abort listener (#81)
eligibility: parent and head pinned runtime suites completed green in the frozen-order extension

review_fields.contract_or_reason: Removes the abort listener on resolve or reject and registers it with {once: true}, fixing a listener leak on long-lived signals. Results are unchanged. With an already-aborted signal the listener is still added after cleanup, but `once` and the aborted state make that harmless. No test.

title: ecoutils: skip identifying lookups when scrubbing (#461)

title: Fix large number overflows for Int() and Uint()
eligibility: parent and head pinned runtime suites completed green in the frozen-order extension

review_fields.contract_or_reason: Changes integer overflow from wrapping to saturating, adds float-string fallback for Int/Uint on strings, and updates the old wraparound assertions. The overflow check (`next < n`) is incomplete: "35000000000000000000" wraps to 16553255926290448384 instead of MaxUint64, so Uint() on large 20-digit numbers stays wrong. That is not a regression (it wrapped before too), but the fix is partial.
